title: Calculate proportion-estimation performance metrics — quasar_prop_metrics
text: inputs must numeric matrices coercible numeric matrices, samples rows cell types columns. intersecting samples cell types retained metric calculation. Let \(\hat{p}_{ic}\) denote estimated proportion sample \(\) cell type \(c\), let \(p_{ic}\) denote corresponding ground-truth proportion. restricting inputs common samples cell types, following metrics calculated. 1. Root mean squared error (RMSE) per cell type cell type \(c\), RMSE calculated across shared samples: $$ \mathrm{RMSE}_c = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^{n}(\hat{p}_{ic} - p_{ic})^2} $$ \(n\) number shared samples. 2. Median absolute deviation (MAD) error per cell type cell type \(c\), error vector first defined \(e_{ic} = \hat{p}_{ic} - p_{ic}\). reported MAD : $$ \mathrm{MAD}_c = \mathrm{median}_i\left(\left|e_{ic} - \mathrm{median}_j(e_{jc})\right|\right) $$ quantifies spread cell-type-specific errors across samples. 3. Normalized mean absolute error (NMAE) per cell type cell type \(c\), mean absolute error normalized range ground-truth proportions across samples: $$ \mathrm{NMAE}_c = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^{n} \frac{|\hat{p}_{ic} - p_{ic}|}{\max_i(p_{ic}) - \min_i(p_{ic})} $$ ground-truth range non-zero. ground-truth range cell type zero, function uses following fallback: returns \(0\) estimated true values identical   samples, otherwise returns unnormalized mean absolute error. 4. Mean ground-truth proportion per cell type cell type \(c\), mean ground-truth proportion : $$ \bar{p}_c = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^{n} p_{ic} $$ 5. Pearson correlation per cell type cell type \(c\), Pearson correlation calculated estimated true proportions across samples: $$ r_c = \mathrm{cor}(\hat{p}_{\cdot c}, p_{\cdot c}) $$ estimated true vector near-zero standard deviation, random noise standard deviation `epsilon` added correlation calculation avoid undefined results constant vectors. 6. Spearman correlation per cell type cell type \(c\), Spearman rank correlation calculated across samples: $$ \rho_c = \mathrm{cor}(\hat{p}_{\cdot c}, p_{\cdot c}, \mathrm{method} = "spearman") $$ Pearson correlation, small perturbation added one vectors near-zero standard deviation. 7. Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) per cell type cell type \(c\), function compares distribution cell type across samples ground truth estimation. Let \(P_c = (p_{1c}, \dots, p_{nc})\) \(Q_c = (\hat{p}_{1c}, \dots, \hat{p}_{nc})\). vectors first normalized sum 1: $$ P_c^* = \frac{P_c}{\sum_i p_{ic}}, \qquad Q_c^* = \frac{Q_c}{\sum_i \hat{p}_{ic}} $$ midpoint distribution : $$ M_c = \frac{1}{2}(P_c^* + Q_c^*) $$ Kullback-Leibler divergence computed : $$ \mathrm{KL}(P \parallel Q) = \sum_k P_k \log\left(\frac{P_k}{Q_k}\right) $$ `epsilon` added internally \(P\) \(Q\) numerical stability. reported Jensen-Shannon distance : $$ \mathrm{JSD}_c = \sqrt{ \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{KL}(P_c^* \parallel M_c) + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{KL}(Q_c^* \parallel M_c) } $$ 8. Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) per sample sample \(\), function compares distribution cell-type proportions across cell types ground truth estimation. Let \(P_i = (p_{i1}, \dots, p_{im})\) \(Q_i = (\hat{p}_{i1}, \dots, \hat{p}_{im})\), \(m\) number shared cell types. normalization sum 1, Jensen-Shannon distance formula applied: $$ \mathrm{JSD}_i = \sqrt{ \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{KL}(P_i^* \parallel M_i) + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{KL}(Q_i^* \parallel M_i) } $$ \(M_i = \frac{1}{2}(P_i^* + Q_i^*)\).
